requirement_text: Foreign upper secondary certificates must meet three cumulative conditions per UZH's Admission Regulations: (1) Educational objective — the certificate must be 'designed as a course specifically geared to university studies but not providing subject-specific or vocational training'; (2) Educational content — must correspond to Swiss standards, with at least 90% general education subjects and at least six continuously-studied subjects in the final three years (first language, foreign language, mathematics, a natural science, a humanities/social science, plus informatics/philosophy/another specified subject); (3) Duration — must align with Swiss maturity certificate duration standards per §16 para. 3 of the Admission Regulations. UZH's own page adds: 'A minimum overall grade determined by the University of Zurich may also have to be achieved' depending on certificate type, without stating the number on this page (deferred to the country-specific list).
source_authority_note: uzh.ch is University of Zurich's official domain; not .edu/.ac./.gov.
limitations: The specific minimum overall grade is not stated on this page and was not separately tracked down for a specific country during this pass — recorded as an acknowledged gap rather than guessed.
researcher_notes: CROSS-CHECK PERFORMED per coordinator instruction: this three-condition structure is consistent with (not contradictory to) the central swissuniversities six-subject framework recorded in the system file (REQ-2026-08-21-0001) — no conflict found. UZH's restatement adds the 90%-general-education and duration-matching conditions as explicit numbered criteria, which is additional detail rather than a contradiction.

requirement_text: CONDITIONAL RECOGNITION (verbatim shape, not a threshold): certificates that only 'partially' match Swiss standards may still permit admission if the applicant provides proof of 'at least two successfully completed years of study' at a state-accredited university in a field also offered in Switzerland (§17 of UZH's Admission Regulations). This is recognition-conditional-on-a-combination (partial certificate + subsequent university study), not a simple pass/fail threshold on the secondary certificate alone.
limitations: The precise definition of 'partially matching' (how partial is still eligible) is not quantified on this page; deferred to case-by-case assessment per §17.
researcher_notes: FLAGGED PER COORDINATOR INSTRUCTION as a genuine conditional-recognition rule (the third rule-shape beyond simple threshold and simple supplementary-exam): recognition here is conditional on a COMBINATION of partial certificate equivalence AND completed university study, recorded verbatim rather than collapsed into either a scored threshold or a flat 'needs ECUS' statement.

requirement_text: Applicants from countries not signatory to the Lisbon Recognition Convention 'must, as a rule, also pass the complementary examination of the Swiss higher education institutions (ECUS)' in order to gain admission. Because ECUS is held only in August each year, this effectively restricts affected applicants to Fall-semester entry only.
limitations: 'As a rule' (per the source's own qualifying language) implies exceptions exist but are not enumerated on this page.
researcher_notes: Supplementary-exam-shaped rule, consistent with (not contradicting) the central ECUS description in the Switzerland-system file (REQ-2026-08-21-0004/0005) — cross-check performed, no conflict found.

requirement_text: Non-Swiss applicants must demonstrate German language skills of at least level C1 (CEFR).
limitations: Most undergraduate programs at UZH are taught in German; this C1 requirement applies to the general/most-programs case — specific English-taught programs (if any) were not separately researched in this pass.

requirement_text: UZH's own admission page directs applicants to swissuniversities.ch for country-specific requirements, explicitly noting these are 'updated annually' and apply 'exclusively to the year of study indicated' — i.e. UZH treats the swissuniversities country list as the authoritative, year-specific source of truth for foreign-certificate details, rather than restating every country's figures on its own page.
researcher_notes: This is a data point in favor of the 'national coordination' side of the governance picture (system file REQ-2026-08-21-0002): UZH explicitly defers to swissuniversities' country list rather than maintaining an independent one, for country-level specifics. No conflict found between UZH's page and the swissuniversities central page on this point — they agree UZH follows the central list.

requirement_text: Applicants to UZH's Bachelor Medicine must meet two conditions: (1) 'über die schweizerische oder liechtensteinische Staatsbürgerschaft oder über einen entsprechenden Aufenthaltsstatus verfügt' (hold Swiss or Liechtenstein citizenship, or an equivalent residence status), AND (2) meet standard UZH bachelor admission requirements. 'Falls der Regierungsrat Zulassungsbeschränkungen anordnet, erfolgt die Studienplatzvergabe in Koordination mit den anderen Schweizer Hochschulen' (if the [cantonal] Regierungsrat orders enrollment restrictions, place allocation happens in coordination with the other Swiss universities) — i.e. via the centralized EMS/swissuniversities process.
limitations: Original text in German; English gloss provided is a translation performed during research, not an official UZH translation.
researcher_notes: Consistent with the Switzerland-system file's general EMS citizenship/residence restriction (REQ-2026-08-21-0007) — no conflict found.

requirement_text: 'Nicht fristgerecht eingereichte Anmeldungen werden nicht berücksichtigt' (applications not submitted by the deadline will not be considered). Applicants must provide UZH with a confirmation copy of their swissuniversities registration during the UZH online application; an incomplete UZH application precludes participation in the medicine admission process entirely, regardless of swissuniversities/EMS registration status.
researcher_notes: Important procedural trap: applicants must complete BOTH the national swissuniversities/MEDON registration AND UZH's own separate online application — neither alone is sufficient.

requirement_text: Application fee for Bachelor's studies at UZH is CHF 100 generally; from 1 January 2025, applicants with foreign qualifications pay CHF 150.
limitations: This fee figure came from a WebSearch summary rather than a direct WebFetch of the official fee page during this research pass — recorded with low confidence and flagged NEEDS_REVIEW rather than silently treated as equally reliable to the WebFetch-sourced records above. Recommend an official-page WebFetch to confirm before relying on this figure.
researcher_notes: Deliberately downgraded confidence/verification_state because this particular fact's strongest source was a WebSearch AI summary, not a verified WebFetch of the primary page — flagging the provenance gap explicitly rather than presenting it with the same confidence as verbatim/WebFetch-sourced facts elsewhere in this file.

limitations: Page did not differentiate this deadline by applicant nationality/diploma origin despite being asked to; appears to be a single deadline for all standard Bachelor applicants regardless of certificate origin (visa-required applicants have their own earlier deadline — see DL-2026-08-21-0303).

limitations: Consistent with UZH's own German-language medicine page, which separately stated 'UZH online application period is January 1 to March 31' for the 2026/2027 cycle — cross-checked, no conflict. 'For medicine no applications are possible for spring semester' per the same source.

limitations: The extended Dec 1-Jan 31 window is restricted to applicants who already hold a Swiss university entrance qualification, so is not generally available to first-time international applicants.
